# kite

> kite is a single-binary, dependency-free Kafka CLI (under 1 MB, written in Zig) that produces stdin lines to a topic and consumes a topic to stdout. It is built for scripts, containers, CI, and AI agents: no JVM, no librdkafka, no daemon, no prompts, and piped reads terminate on idle by default.

Consumer groups (Kafka 4.0): `kite group list [--all] [--json]` lists consumer groups on every broker (`--all` includes classic groups), warning on partial results. `kite group describe GROUP [--json]` shows group/topic/partition/committed/end/lag/member_id/client_id; classic groups show offsets only, with empty member/client IDs. Missing commits or unavailable end/lag are `-` in TSV, null in JSON. Lag is clamped to zero after truncation and measured against the high watermark (read_uncommitted). Both commands accept @CLUSTER and common flags. These commands do not modify group offsets.

Repository: https://github.com/addisonhuddy/kite
License: Apache-2.0
Platforms: Linux x86_64/aarch64, macOS x86_64/arm64
Brokers: any Kafka-protocol broker (Apache Kafka, Confluent Cloud, Redpanda, Amazon MSK with SASL/SCRAM, Aiven, WarpStream)
Security: PLAINTEXT, SSL, SASL_SSL, SASL_PLAINTEXT; SASL PLAIN, SCRAM-SHA-256, SCRAM-SHA-512
Scope: produce, consume, topic management (list/create/delete/update), consumer group consumption and inspection. kite does not reset/delete groups, manage ACLs, or administer clusters.

`kite consume -g GROUP TOPIC` / `--group GROUP` joins a Kafka 4.0 consumer-protocol group, shares partitions, resumes commits, and commits the flushed fetch position (last emitted + 1 when -n stops mid-batch). Commits have a 1s floor, bypassed on revoke/exit. `-B` applies only without an existing commit; otherwise a new partition starts at latest. Conflicts: --offset, --partition. A commit means stdout accepted the record, NOT that the downstream reader processed it. Drain stdout within the session timeout (45s default) to avoid fencing/replay. Failed output rounds are not committed; crashes can replay records. Idle/-n/SIGINT commit flushed progress and leave; broken pipe leaves without committing the failed round. Group idle starts at the first assignment heartbeat, including an empty assignment; zero-partition members exit after the idle window unless --follow. Without -g consume remains independent and never commits. -v logs joins/assignments/commits.

Use one isolation mode per group. Mixing the default with --read-uncommitted can commit past records still hidden from read-committed members and make lag misleading. To replay after switching isolation modes, use a fresh group with -B; existing groups resume committed offsets.

## Install

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/addisonhuddy/kite/main/install.sh | sh
Options: --bin-dir DIR (or KITE_BIN_DIR), --version vX.Y.Z (or KITE_VERSION). Release checksums (SHA256SUMS) are verified.
From source: zig build (Zig 0.16.x).

## Configure

Precedence: flags > environment > properties file.
-b HOST:PORT[,HOST:PORT]        brokers
BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS               brokers
SECURITY_PROTOCOL               PLAINTEXT | SSL | SASL_SSL | SASL_PLAINTEXT
SASL_MECHANISM                  PLAIN | SCRAM-SHA-256 | SCRAM-SHA-512
SASL_USERNAME, SASL_PASSWORD
SSL_TRUSTSTORE_LOCATION         optional PEM CA bundle
--config FILE                   config file (also $KAFKA_PROPERTIES, ./kite.yaml, ./kite.properties, ~/.config/kite/)
@NAME                           named cluster from kite.yaml's `clusters:` (this run only)
kite cluster                    interactive picker (TTY) or the same output as `list`
kite cluster list [--json]      list clusters, `*` marks the effective one; never connects
kite cluster set NAME           store NAME as the current cluster (beats `default:`)
kite cluster init               wizard: add a cluster to kite.yaml by answering questions
kite -v                         verbose: prints which config sources were used
kite update [VERSION]           replace this binary with the latest (or VERSION) GitHub release

## Produce

kite produce [OPTIONS] [@CLUSTER] TOPIC   one stdin line = one record
  value                         plain value
  key<TAB>value                 keyed record
  key<TAB>name: v<TAB>value     with headers
--json                          JSON records; non-string value sent verbatim; key_b64/value_b64 and array-header value_b64 decode padded standard base64
--csv [--key COL]               RFC 4180 CSV rows -> JSON object values, optional key column
-H 'name: value'                header on every record (repeatable)
--txn ID                        produce all of stdin atomically under transactional ID (commits on EOF, aborts on error or interrupt before commit; if interrupted after commit is sent, exits 130 reporting unknown outcome instead of aborting; requires enable.idempotence=true)
Produce is batched and idempotent by default. stdout is never written.

## Topics

kite topic [list]                 one topic name per line, sorted (aligned table on a terminal); -a includes internal topics
kite topic list --json            {"name","partitions","replication_factor","internal"} per line
kite topic create [-p N] [-r N] [-s KEY=VALUE]... [--if-not-exists] TOPIC
kite topic update [-p N] [--set KEY=VALUE]... [--unset KEY]... TOPIC   (partitions can only grow)
kite topic delete [-y] [--if-exists] TOPIC...   -y required when stderr is not a terminal

## Consume

kite consume [OPTIONS] [@CLUSTER] TOPIC   records on stdout
-B, --from-beginning            earliest offset (default: latest for the isolation level)
--offset N  --partition P       start offset / single partition
-n, --max N                     stop after N records
-t, --idle DUR                  stop after DUR without records (3s, 500ms, 1m)
-f, --follow                    never stop on idle
--read-uncommitted              include open and aborted transactional records
--json                          UTF-8 JSON per record; invalid UTF-8 key/value/header bytes use sibling *_b64 fields (standard padded base64), safe for jq
Default when stdout is a pipe or file: stop after 5 s idle, so scripts never hang.
Default isolation, also with -g: read committed (stop at the last stable offset and skip aborted transactions). --read-uncommitted reads to the high watermark. Neither mode prints transaction markers.
An open transaction can hold records behind the last stable offset even with -B: consume may exit 0 with no records and an (idle timeout) summary (suppressed by -q). Use --follow instead of --idle to keep waiting for the transaction to resolve.

## Contract

stdout: data only. stderr: diagnostics and end-of-run summary.
Exit 0 success; 1 any error with one line "kite: MESSAGE"; 130 on Ctrl-C.
No interactive prompts. No color unless a TTY (NO_COLOR / KITE_COLOR honored). No files written.
-q suppresses summaries; -v adds connection/retry diagnostics; KITE_DEBUG=1 adds frame/TLS traces.

## Schema Registry (wing)

wing is a separate CLI for Confluent Schema Registry and JSON Schema; kite itself never connects to the Registry.
Pipe `wing write TOPIC` before `kite produce --json TOPIC` to validate and add the schema header, or `kite consume --json TOPIC | wing read` to decode and validate.
Records remain kite `--json` JSONL; kite v0.4.0+ preserves binary schema headers through jq using `_b64` fields.
Configure them separately: kite uses `BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS`; wing uses `SCHEMA_REGISTRY_URL` or `wing.yaml`. Avro and Protobuf are not supported by either.

## Examples

printf 'hello\n' | kite produce -b localhost:9092 events
kite consume -B -n 100 --idle 3s events
kite consume -B --json events | jq -c .value
kite consume -B --json src | kite produce --json dst
kite consume -B -n 2 --idle 3s --json orders | wing read | jq -c .value
kite produce --csv --key user_id events < users.csv
tail -f app.log | kite produce logs
